A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same cyclic-consistency approach to adversarial MRI reconstruction despite the changed title. Their complete main texts and supplements, including figures, tables and equations, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original fastMRI reconstruction and attack-detection experiments, including PSNR/SSIM measurements, visual comparisons and supplementary ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original MRI experiments and adds adaptive-attack evaluations, mitigation examples for clean inputs and associated analyses.

M1.justification: v1 Algorithm 2 applies an Adam-style momentum transformation before the sign-gradient update; v2 Algorithm 1 uses the gradient sign directly. This changes the optimizer while retaining the central cyclic-consistency objective, blind-search procedure and detection algorithm, which moves to the supplement.

E1.justification: v2 adds defense-aware adaptive attacks, introducing a materially different adversary-knowledge scenario. It removes Cor-PDFS knee coverage from the dataset description, reconstruction results and detection plots, while retaining Cor-PD knee and Ax-FLAIR brain data. Existing supervised, FGSM, k-space and non-uniform-sampling scenarios remain.

E2.justification: The comparator set remains SMUG, the two adversarial-training variants and their mitigation combinations. However, Eq. (6), evaluated in supplementary Table 4, changes from maximizing an expected loss to taking the expectation of an inner maximum. This revises the reported comparator formulation; unchanged Table 4 scores do not establish retraining.

E3.justification: The new adaptive evaluation uses 75 Cor-PD slices, attack unroll counts of 10, 25, 50 and 100, and both matched-unroll and convergence-based mitigation. It also introduces attack-weight tuning and gradient checks. The stated blind step-size schedule changes from epsilon/2.5 through epsilon/5.5 in v1's main text to epsilon through epsilon/3.5 in v2.

E4.justification: v2 adds adaptive-attack sensitivity to unroll depth and attack weight, gradient-obfuscation checks comparing attack algorithms and strengths, and clean-input mitigation examples. The existing analysis of reconstruction-stage count is retained in supplementary Section 10 and Figure 14; its relocation is not a new ablation.

E5.justification: Both versions report population PSNR/SSIM summaries and detection violin plots with medians and quartiles. Neither reports repeated-run uncertainty, seed variation, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added convergence-iteration averages do not introduce an uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Several mitigation scores change: Table 1's Cor-PD proposed-plus-MoDL PSNR changes from 33.23 to 35.14, while supplementary Table 2's epsilon=0.02 proposed-plus-AT PSNR changes from 35.65 to 33.42. These accompany the optimizer revision. Cor-PDFS entries disappear, and adaptive-attack and clean-input findings are added. The adaptive results use a separate subset and should not be directly compared with full-population scores.

T1.justification: v2 introduces the adaptive-attack optimization formulation in Eqs. (11)-(12), adds the image-to-k-space perturbation derivation and explicitly states the multi-coil dimensional assumption. Eq. (6) also changes the order of expectation and maximization. No new theorem or proof appears; Eq. (15) formalizes the already-described multi-stage ablation.

C1.justification: Detection is removed from the title and principal contribution list, although retained as a complementary supplementary method. The abstract, introduction and conclusion add an explicit claim of robustness against attackers who know the defense. Training-free mitigation, blindness to attack parameters and compatibility with robust training remain core claims.

C2.justification: New Section 2.4 explains why adversarial attacks matter as stability probes despite limited opportunities for malicious injection into MRI pipelines. v2 also adds explanations for clean-input convergence and adaptive robustness, discusses failures with few mitigation unrolls, and attributes increasing attack-strength problems in adversarial training to its fixed training strength.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies SMUG's sampling count and noise level, adversarial-training PGD parameters and normalization, normalized cyclic-loss implementation, and adaptive-gradient checkpointing and fixed-noise handling. It also reconciles the conflicting blind-search schedules previously stated in v1's main text and supplement. Newly disclosed baseline settings alone do not establish changed experiments.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning around adaptive attacks and gradient obfuscation, including work by Athalye, Tramer, Chen and others. Section 2.4 adds literature on reconstruction instability, motion, hardware artifacts and clinical relevance. These additions broaden the scientific rationale and evaluation standards beyond v1's emphasis on reconstruction and robust training.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized around mitigation: the paper is retitled, the abstract and contribution list are revised, detection moves to the supplement, and the full stage-ablation discussion moves there as well. The supplement changes from Sections A-B to Sections 6-10, integrating implementation, detection, adaptive attacks and ablation material.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn, with its detection panel separated into supplementary Figure 6. Detection plots are consolidated, Cor-PDFS panels are removed, reconstruction and blind-search examples are revised, and clean-input and adaptive-attack displays are added. Tables are extensively restyled, and several existing displays are relocated.

improvement.justification: Adaptive-attack evaluations, clean-input tests, gradient checks and clearer implementation details improve empirical support and reproducibility. However, Cor-PDFS coverage is lost, and revised main results are not reconciled with retained supplementary scores: AT plus mitigation is 36.57 dB in v2 Table 1 but 36.17 dB in supplementary Table 4, without an explained setting difference. These tradeoffs limit the net quality gain.
